title: Company-wide policies and process documentation - Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendor, Travel, Templates
author: Asha Patel
content:
Purpose:
This page centralizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and the canonical internal templates. It is intended as the single-point-of-truth for process owners, approvers, and auditors.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, consultants, and vendors with access to Redwood systems or data.
- Operational coverage: hosted API, Dedicated clusters, Private deployments, internal developer platforms, and all internal business systems.

Owners and Contacts:
- Policy owner: People Ops (owner_team)
- Primary contact: Asha Patel (People Ops) — asha.patel@redwood.ai
- Security review: Security & Compliance (Sophie Kline)
- Finance approvals and thresholds: Finance & Legal (Rajiv Menon)

1) Access & Permissions
Overview:
Redwood enforces least-privilege access across cloud, infra, and business systems. Access requests must follow the Access Request flow below. Elevated or emergency access is time-limited and logged.

Key controls and SLAs:
- Role-based access control (RBAC) is the default for production systems.
- Provisioning SLA: 3 business days for standard requests.
- Emergency access SLA: 4 hours (requires on-call owner + two approvers).
- Quarterly access reviews for privileged groups (owners: team leads + security).

Access request flow (standard):
1. Requester files an Access Request using the Access Request template (see Templates section).
2. Requester’s manager approves scope and business justification.
3. System owner (service owner) approves and assigns role.
4. Identity & Access team provisions access and records request in the audit log.

Emergency access flow:
1. Request via Emergency Access form (flagged in system).
2. SRE/security on-call provides temporary credentials valid for a maximum of 8 hours.
3. Post-event review required within 3 business days.

Example IAM policy snippet (for reference):
# (YAML formatted example - do not copy directly into prod)
policy: |
  Version: "2012-10-17"
  Statement:
    - Effect: Allow
      Action:
        - ec2:DescribeInstances
      Resource: "*"
      Condition:
        StringEquals:
          aws:PrincipalTag/Team: "infra"

2) Change Management
Principles:
- All non-trivial changes impacting production (compute, model endpoints, configs, infra) require a Change Request and categorization.
- Regular changes are planned and reviewed by the Change Advisory Board (CAB).

Change categories and approval matrix:
- Standard change: low-risk, pre-approved (e.g., routine config updates) — no CAB review required; owner approval only.
- Normal change: medium risk — requires CAB + system-owner sign-off.
- Emergency change: requires emergency CAB (on-call) and post-facto documentation.

CAB cadence and SLAs:
- CAB meetings weekly (Tues 10:00–11:00 PST).
- Normal change review SLA: schedule within 2 business days.
- Deployment windows: Mon–Fri 02:00–08:00 UTC (default).

Change Request template fields (required):
- Change title, owner, risk classification, rollback plan, impact window, pre- and post-checks, monitoring & alerting hooks, and stakeholder list.

Rollback and verification:
- Every change must include an automated rollback or manual rollback checklist and verification steps.
- Post-change verification: 30-minute health check followed by 24-hour observation for regressions.

Change freeze policy:
- Two-week change freeze before major product releases and on defined blackout dates (calendar published by Product). Exceptions handled by emergency CAB.

3) Data Management
Classification:
- Data is classified as Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted.
- Default classification: Internal.

Handling rules per class:
- Public: can be published externally. No PII or IP.
- Internal: internal use only; encryption in transit required.
- Confidential: encryption at rest + in transit; access limited to approved roles.
- Restricted: high-sensitivity (customer PHI/PCI/regulated data) — requires Private deployment option and legal review.

Retention and deletion:
- Standard logs: retention 90 days.
- Analytics aggregates: 2 years.
- Backups: 30-day snapshot retention; long-term archived snapshots retained 7 years for compliance cases.
- Data deletion requests: follow the Data Deletion Procedure; product owner must respond within 10 business days.

Encryption and backups:
- All production data at rest must be encrypted with customer-managed KMS where required.
- Daily backups; RPO target: 24 hours; RTO target: 8 hours for core services.

Data access review and audit:
- Quarterly audit of privileged access to Confidential and Restricted datasets.
- Security retains audit logs for 365 days in a tamper-evident store.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Procurement thresholds and approval matrix:
- Under $5k: Manager approval.
- $5k–$50k: Manager + Finance approval.
- > $50k: Manager + Finance + Legal approval and a PO.
- Recurring commitments: must include a 12-month total cost estimate and owner.

Expense policy highlights:
- Travel per diem (US): $200/day (meals & incidentals), lodging reimbursed at actuals with receipt up to $350/night in major metros, higher caps require approval.
- Expense submission SLA: 30 days from spend; after 90 days claims require a justification and senior approval.

Procurement process (high level):
1. Create a Procurement Request using the Procurement Request template.
2. Finance validates budget and assigns GL codes.
3. Contracts & Legal review for >$50k or vendors storing customer data.
4. PO issued and procurement executed.

Vendor payment terms:
- Standard: Net-30. Exceptions documented and approved by Finance and Legal.

5) Vendor Management
Vendor classification:
- Low risk: Off-the-shelf SaaS with no customer data.
- Medium risk: Vendors with business data integration.
- High risk: Vendors that process customer data, model artifacts, or have elevated access.

Onboarding checklist (minimum):
- Vendor profile creation (vendor owner, contract dates, contact info).
- Security questionnaire (based on our Vendor Risk Assessment).
- Contract clauses: data processing agreement (DPA), security addenda, SLAs.
- SOC2 or equivalent evidence for High-risk vendors.

Ongoing monitoring:
- Annual reviews for Medium/High vendors.
- Security incidents: vendors must report incidents within 72 hours.

Termination and offboarding:
- Data return or certified deletion clause must be exercised.
- Access keys revoked and verified.

6) Travel Policies
Pre-approval and booking:
- All business travel requires manager pre-approval via Travel Request template.
- Use preferred travel vendors for corporate rates and insurance coverage.

Safety and insurance:
- International travel requires GeoRisk check and insurance enrollment.
- Emergency contact (People Ops) available 24/7 for business travel incidents.

Expense reporting:
- Submit expenses within 30 days with itemized receipts.
- Corporate cards should be used where issued; reconciliations monthly.

7) Internal Templates (canonical links and usage)
Templates available (Confluence + Google Drive canonical copies):
- Access Request template — /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/access-request-template
- Change Request template — /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/change-request-template
- Procurement Request / PO template — /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/procurement-request-template
- Emergency Access form — /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/emergency-access-form
- Travel Request & Expense template — /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/travel-request-template
- Vendor Risk Assessment questionnaire — /confluence/policies-and-process/templates/vendor-risk-assessment

Process instrumentation and tooling:
- Access requests are tracked in the Identity system (Okta + internal provisioning tickets).
- Change Requests tracked in the Change Management board (Jira project: CHANGE).
- Procurement requests tracked via SpendDesk / Finance tooling; exceptions logged in the Procurement board.

Enforcement, Audit and Exceptions:
- Periodic audits: People Ops + Security + Finance run an annual cross-functional audit.
- Exception process: documented risks require an owner, compensating controls, and approval by appropriate stakeholders (Security/Finance/Product).

FAQs and common scenarios:
Q: Who approves vendor contracts storing customer data?
A: Finance + Legal + Security must review; the vendor is classified as Medium/High risk and requires a DPA.

Q: How do I request temporary elevated access for a production debugging session?
A: Submit the Emergency Access form and contact on-call SRE/security; temporary credentials will be issued for up to 8 hours with a post-event review.
